subject: Ministry of Forests branches and regions
meaning: An explicitly May 2001 organization chart names Policy and Economics, Operations, Forestry and Management Services divisions; branches include Protection, Business Improvement, Forest Enterprises, Timber Supply, Resources Inventory and Forestry Division Services, among others. It also names Vancouver, Prince Rupert, Prince George, Kamloops, Nelson and Cariboo forest regions. The chart is evidence for adding historical nodes; nested edges should be transcribed visually before import.
locator: PDF p. 12, organization chart headed May 2001

subject: Gaming Policy and Enforcement Branch divisions
meaning: The annual report describes Policy, Legislation and Standards; Licensing and Grants; Racing; Registration; Audit and Compliance; and Investigation divisions within the branch. These are candidate subordinate nodes, not present in the compiled queue.
locator: PDF pp. 21–22, Gaming Policy and Enforcement Branch

subject: BCCDC Public Health Emergency Management program
meaning: BCCDC’s report describes its Public Health Emergency Management program as established in 2007. Do not merge this program with Health Emergency Management BC solely because names and emergency functions overlap.
locator: PDF p. 33, Public Health Emergency Management

subject: Energy and Environmental Sustainability shared service
meaning: The 2015 environmental accountability report retrospectively says the Energy and Environmental Sustainability team was created in 2010 as a Lower Mainland health-authority consolidated service. Shared-service governance needs a separate relationship model.

subject: British Columbia Government Travel Bureau
meaning: The Department of Recreation and Conservation Act explicitly establishes a bureau by this name in section 8, unlike its broader parks-function language. This is a useful historical node to investigate with commencement rules and successor records.
locator: Act c. 53, section 8; title assent date

subject: Class A and Class B park advisory boards
meaning: The Park Act continues existing parks and Class C boards but dissolves Class A/B advisory boards in section 33. This is institutional discontinuity, not a founding date for all park bodies.
locator: Act c. 31, section 33; title assent date
